content.title: About
content.content: Queso Anejo is an aged Mexican cheese made from cow’s milk, maturing for 3 to 12 months. During aging it develops a firm, crystalline texture, bright orange hue, and a strong nutty‑caramel flavor with a hint of sharpness.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The word “anejo” means “old” in Spanish, highlighting its long aging period.
Traditionally produced in the Mexican states of Oaxaca and Chiapas, where the climate favors slow maturation.
Tyrosine crystals form during aging, giving the cheese its characteristic crunchy “grainy” sensation.
Often grated over tacos, enchiladas, and guacamole to add depth of flavor.
When tightly wrapped, the cheese can be stored for up to a year in the refrigerator.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Queso Anejo contains more calcium than most soft cheeses, supporting bone and dental health.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: A serving provides about 20 g of high‑quality protein, aiding muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The cheese supplies vitamin B12, riboflavin, and niacin, which are important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Probiotic properties
items.content: Fermentation promotes beneficial bacteria that may help maintain a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Low lactose content
items.content: Extended aging breaks down most lactose, making the cheese more tolerable for people with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to casein or whey may experience reactions ranging from mild to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: The cheese is salty; those with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Because of its high fat content, Queso Anejo is calorie‑dense; moderation is key for weight management.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: A large proportion of the fat is saturated, so people with elevated cholesterol should limit intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Grate Queso Anejo over tortillas, add it to soups, salads, and casseroles, or serve small chunks as a snack with fruit or nuts. For maximum aroma, grate the cheese using a coarse grater just before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cheese in an airtight container or wrapped in wax paper in the refrigerator at 2‑4 °C. For longer storage (over 3 months) it can be frozen, though the texture will become more crumbly.
